description_en: A fermented haritaki-based tonic traditionally used for piles and constipation.
anupana: Equal quantity of warm water after meals
safety_note: Arishta/asava are self-fermented and contain some alcohol; use caution with alcohol avoidance, liver disease, pregnancy and diabetes (sugar/jaggery base).
evidence_note: Evidence is mostly traditional use plus lab or small studies; no robust clinical trials of the specific formulation.

description_en: A guduchi-based fermented preparation traditionally used for fevers and indigestion.
anupana: Equal quantity of warm water after meals
safety_note: Arishta/asava are self-fermented and contain some alcohol; use caution with alcohol avoidance, liver disease, pregnancy and diabetes (sugar/jaggery base).
evidence_note: Guduchi has some small-trial support for fever and immunity, but this formulation has no clinical trials.

description_en: A fermented ashwagandha tonic traditionally used for nervous weakness and vitality.
anupana: Equal quantity of warm water after meals
safety_note: Arishta/asava are self-fermented and contain some alcohol; use caution with alcohol avoidance, liver disease, pregnancy and diabetes (sugar/jaggery base). Ashwagandha: avoid in pregnancy; reports of liver injury and thyroid effects; may add to sedatives.
evidence_note: Ashwagandha has limited human trial data (stress, anxiety); the arishta itself is unstudied.

description_en: A bala-based fermented tonic traditionally used for nerve and joint complaints and strength.
anupana: Equal quantity of warm water after meals
safety_note: Arishta/asava are self-fermented and contain some alcohol; use caution with alcohol avoidance, liver disease, pregnancy and diabetes (sugar/jaggery base). Contains ashwagandha: avoid in pregnancy.
evidence_note: Evidence is mostly traditional use plus lab or small studies; no robust clinical trials of the specific formulation.

description_en: A widely used fermented dashamoola tonic for joint pain, respiratory complaints and post-natal recovery.
anupana: Equal quantity of warm water after meals
safety_note: Arishta/asava are self-fermented and contain some alcohol; use caution with alcohol avoidance, liver disease, pregnancy and diabetes (sugar/jaggery base). Commonly used post-partum, but use under physician guidance.
evidence_note: Evidence is mostly traditional use plus lab or small studies; no robust clinical trials of the specific formulation.

description_en: A brahmi-based fermented tonic traditionally used to support memory and calm the mind.
anupana: Equal quantity of warm water after meals
safety_note: Arishta/asava are self-fermented and contain some alcohol; use caution with alcohol avoidance, liver disease, pregnancy and diabetes (sugar/jaggery base). Parsed record lists processed gold; this version contains Acorus calamus (vacha), which has regulatory restrictions in some countries.
evidence_note: Bacopa has limited and inconsistent evidence for memory; the formulation itself is untested.

description_en: An aloe-based fermented tonic traditionally used for menstrual problems and uterine health.
anupana: Equal quantity of warm water after meals
safety_note: Arishta/asava are self-fermented and contain some alcohol; use caution with alcohol avoidance, liver disease, pregnancy and diabetes (sugar/jaggery base). Contains processed iron; avoid in pregnancy unless advised.
evidence_note: Evidence is mostly traditional use plus lab or small studies; no robust clinical trials of the specific formulation.

description_en: The classic amla-based herbal jam used as a daily rejuvenating tonic for immunity and respiratory health.
safety_note: Contains sugar and honey: caution in diabetes. Heavy-metal content has been questioned for some Ayurvedic products; one 2011 consumer test found major brands acceptable.
evidence_note: Widely used; small studies on immunity and respiratory outcomes exist but high-quality trials are scarce.

description_en: A ghee-and-honey based rejuvenative preparation traditionally taken to improve vitality, memory and longevity.
safety_note: Contains sugar and honey: caution in diabetes.
evidence_note: Only traditional use plus limited preclinical research; no solid clinical trials found.

description_en: A herbal jam traditionally used for cough, asthma and other respiratory disorders.
safety_note: Contains jaggery, ghee and honey: caution in diabetes.
evidence_note: Traditional use only; no robust clinical trials found.

description_en: A medicated ghee traditionally used for memory, mental disorders and speech problems.
safety_note: Ghee base: caution with high cholesterol. Bacopa may cause nausea and gut upset.
evidence_note: Bacopa has limited and inconsistent evidence for cognition; this ghee is untested clinically.

description_en: A medicated ghee traditionally used for mental disorders, reproductive problems and general nourishment.
safety_note: Ghee base: caution with high cholesterol; physician supervision advised for epilepsy or infertility.
evidence_note: Traditional use only; no robust clinical trials found.

description_en: A bitter medicated ghee traditionally used for skin diseases and blood purification.
anupana: Warm water; also used in classical purification therapy
safety_note: Ghee base: caution with high cholesterol.
evidence_note: Traditional use only; limited small studies.

description_en: A sesame-oil based medicated oil for nerve and joint disorders, used externally and in vasti.
anupana: External application, nasya, vasti, pichu, dhara
safety_note: Mainly external; avoid on broken skin or in fever and acute inflammation unless advised.
evidence_note: Traditional use only; small studies on oil massage are low quality.

description_en: A classic medicated oil for musculoskeletal and neurological complaints, widely used in infant and post-natal massage.
anupana: External application, also nasya, vasti and oral use under supervision
safety_note: Mainly external; patch-test first; oral use only under supervision.
evidence_note: Traditional use only; no robust clinical trials found.

description_en: A black-gram based medicated oil traditionally used for paralytic and nerve disorders.
safety_note: Mainly external; patch-test first.
evidence_note: Traditional use only; no robust clinical trials found.

description_en: A medicated oil applied externally for rheumatic pain, cramps and swelling.
safety_note: External use only; garlic may irritate sensitive skin; patch-test.
evidence_note: Traditional use only; no robust clinical trials found.

description_en: A multi-ingredient tablet traditionally used for urinary and genito-urinary disorders.
anupana: Warm milk, honey or Brihatyadi kashaya
safety_note: Contains shilajit and guggulu; metal content concerns generally apply to Ayurvedic mineral products; guggul may affect thyroid and drug metabolism (CYP3A4); caution in pregnancy.
evidence_note: Traditional use with a few small trials in urinary symptoms and diabetes, low quality.

description_en: A guggulu tablet traditionally used for skin disease, gout and chronic wounds.
safety_note: Guggul can interact with CYP3A4 drugs, affect thyroid tests, cause GI upset, and rarely liver injury; caution in pregnancy.
evidence_note: Traditional use only; guggul evidence mixed.

description_en: A guggulu tablet traditionally used for thyroid swellings, cysts and tumours.
safety_note: Guggul may alter thyroid hormones and CYP3A4 drug levels; see physician if on thyroid medication or in pregnancy.
evidence_note: Traditional use only; no robust clinical trials found.

description_en: A triphala and guggul tablet traditionally used for piles, fistula and swelling.
safety_note: Guggul may interact with CYP3A4 drugs and thyroid tests; caution in pregnancy.
evidence_note: Traditional use only; triphala has small studies, guggul evidence is mixed.

description_en: A classical guggulu tablet traditionally used for arthritis and joint pain.
safety_note: Some versions contain metals (bhasma) in the full classical recipe; guggul may interact with CYP3A4 drugs and thyroid tests; caution in pregnancy.
evidence_note: Traditional use; a few small trials in arthritis, low quality.

description_en: A guggulu tablet with punarnava traditionally used for swelling and joint complaints.
safety_note: Guggul may interact with CYP3A4 drugs and thyroid tests; caution in pregnancy.
evidence_note: Traditional use only; no robust clinical trials found.

description_en: A bitter multi-herb powder traditionally used for fevers and indigestion.
safety_note: Very bitter; may upset the stomach; caution in pregnancy.
evidence_note: Traditional use; limited small studies of components such as Andrographis.

description_en: A three-pungent-spice powder used to kindle digestion and clear respiratory congestion.
safety_note: Pungent; may aggravate acidity or ulcers; piperine can increase absorption of some drugs.
evidence_note: Mostly traditional use plus piperine bioavailability research.

description_en: A digestive powder with asafoetida traditionally used for indigestion, gas and constipation.
safety_note: Contains alkaline salts; caution with hyperacidity; avoid in pregnancy unless advised.
evidence_note: Traditional use only; no robust clinical trials found.
